text:
alex_support: FYI customer reported a metering delta — their internal audit shows ~120k tokens for 2026-11-03 00:00-06:00 UTC but our private dashboard shows ~73k. They think events dropped in the VPC agent.

marta_ops: Thanks. Which on-prem agent version are they running? Any recent restarts?

alex_support: v2.3.1, deployed as a k8s DaemonSet in their VPC. They restarted the pod once around 02:15 UTC for an unrelated config roll.

meter-agent-bot: ALERT: agent-ingest low-throughput detected for cluster acme-prod at 02:14:58 UTC (ingest_rate drop 58%). Persistent queue length spiked to 42.

sam_eng_ml: Can we get the agent logs around the restart? Need to check for seq_id gaps / dedupe during replay. Also confirm system clock on node. Clock skew + negative timestamps can cause dropped events in the pipeline.

alex_support: Pasted logs from customer (redacted) — they sent this snippet:

```
2026-11-03T02:14:50Z INFO queueing event seq=348901 sender=token-meter
2026-11-03T02:14:52Z WARN persist_queue flush failed: write EIO
2026-11-03T02:14:55Z INFO agent shutdown requested
2026-11-03T02:15:12-0500 INFO starting agent v2.3.1 (k8s) seq_resume=348901
2026-11-03T02:15:13Z INFO replaying 41 events from local queue
2026-11-03T02:15:14Z ERROR publish failed: remote-3.redwood.svc:400 proto mismatch, dropping event seq=348912
```

marta_ops: Interesting: see the timestamp with -0500 on the restart line. That node was reporting local time instead of UTC when systemd restarted the container. Could explain out-of-order timestamps.

quinn_sre: If the agent uses the local timestamp as part of the dedupe/ordering key, a restart that flips to local TZ can cause seq resume to appear older/newer to the collector and trigger discard. Need to confirm whether the collector accepts out-of-order seq with a tolerance window.

sam_eng_ml: I dug into the serving runtime docs — collector will accept sequence numbers beyond the last ack but will drop events with timestamp < last_ack_ts - 5s (safety window). If node clock jumped backward by >5s, replayed events might be rejected as "stale".

alex_support: Customer says their node NTP was misconfigured; chronyd was not running after the update. They fixed NTP around 02:20 UTC.

marta_ops: That matches. Two likely contributors: 1) persist queue write EIO caused local queueing + later replay, 2) node clock jump (UTC vs -0500) caused collector to treat replayed events as stale and drop them.

sam_eng_ml: Quick repro steps we should ask the customer to run:
- grep for "persist_queue" and "replaying" in agent logs for window
- check agent local queue count: /var/lib/redwood/agent/queue/metadata.json (seq range)
- run `agentctl snapshot --since 2026-11-03T02:00:00Z --until 2026-11-03T06:00:00Z` and upload to support.

alex_support: Sent repro steps. Also asked for the agent config (time_zone, use_local_time flags).

meter-agent-bot: METRICS: cluster acme-prod — dropped_events=41, replayed_events=0, seq_gaps=4, avg_inflight=1.7

quinn_sre: 41 drops is exactly the spike we saw in persist queue replay. seq_gaps=4 suggests a few events were never enqueued or were deduped earlier.

marta_ops: Ops action plan: 1) ask customer to re-run `agentctl replay --force` after NTP fixed (will resend missing events) 2) temporarily widen server-side timestamp tolerance to 60s for that cluster to accept replays while we validate 3) add a sentinel to the collector to log when events are rejected due to timestamp < last_ack_ts to confirm root cause.

sam_eng_ml: Also filing a runtime bug: treat agent-provided seq_id as primary ordering and use timestamp as advisory. If clock-drift causes rejections we should prefer replay based on seq continuity. Assign to eng-runtime.

alex_support: Customer agreed to replay and is running `agentctl replay --force` now. I'll keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

marta_ops: Nice. After customer confirms we should do invoice reconciliation for 2026-11-03 and mark the missing ~47k tokens as "delivered after replay" if events come through.

alex_support: Update 02:48 UTC — customer reports replay completed, meter-bot shows delivered 43 events. Their dashboard now shows ~118k tokens, close to their audit. I'll log this and close after final invoice reconciliation.

meter-agent-bot: INFO: replay complete for cluster acme-prod. delivered_events=43, errors=0

quinn_sre: Great. Follow-ups: add better NTP health checks to agent (fail open with warning), and add a graceful reordering policy on collector. I'll track in ENG-5612.

sam_eng_ml: I'll pick up ENG-5612 and add unit tests for seq-first reordering.

alex_support: Closing loop with customer. Thanks all! :party:
